articles.summary: A win at home in the first-ever encounterHarder bags a braceTop spot defendedA convincing victory in the Südschlager (battle of the south): On Monday evening...
articles.body:
A win at home in the first-ever encounter

A convincing victory in the Südschlager (battle of the south): On Monday evening, FC Bayern Women secured a 4–0 (2–0) win in their first-ever game against VfB Stuttgart , marking their seventh victory in their seventh Bundesliga match of the season. In the first half, Linda Dallmann (14th minute) and Pernille Harder (16') settled the hosts' nerves with a comfortable 2–0 lead early on. After the break, Klara Bühl lost no time in making it 3–0 (49'), effectively putting the game beyond doubt. Harder was once again on hand to score the fourth goal of the day, completing her brace in the 59th minute. Just before the final whistle, Edna Imade wrapped up what was a one-sided affair with a header (90').

Barcala: "A very good performance over the full 90 minutes!"

José Barcala : "Stuttgart tried to close down the spaces in the centre with their 5-3-2 formation. We found good solutions and developed a strong rhythm for long periods. The key was that we stayed true to our game plan: opening up play down the flanks, getting into the spaces and regaining depth from there. Overall, it was a very good performance over the full 90 minutes."

Bühl: "You could see just how much self-belief and joy there is in our game"

Klara Bühl : "Against Stuttgart, we saw just how much self-belief and joy there is in our game right now. I'm naturally particularly pleased that I was able to both score a goal and provide an assist today. As a team, we want to remain focused and achieve our big goals."

Dallmann & Harder put their side ahead early on

Bayern took the initiative early on: in the fourth minute, following a precise through ball from Harder, Bühl crossed from the left to Imade, but her header posed no real threat to VfB goalkeeper Laura Giuliani. The next chance also fell to the Munich side: following a fine move, Sarah Zadrazil set up Franziska Kett , whose effort from left of centre went just a few centimetres wide of the post. In the 14th minute, the Munich side were finally rewarded: Zadrazil played a great pass to Harder, who drove the attack down the right and sent Sarah Mattner through with a long ball. From the byline, Mattner delivered the ball with pinpoint accuracy into the centre, where Dallmann ran onto it and headed home the cross. Just two minutes later, coach José Barcala 's side doubled their lead: Kett played the ball from the left-hand corner of the penalty area out to Bühl, who, after a one-two with Dallmann, crossed back into the box and all the way through the six-yard box, where Harder was on hand to make it 2–0 (16').

After 20 minutes, the Stuttgart side began to make their presence felt in attack: Yuka Hirano tried her luck from distance, but sent the ball well over the Munich goal. This did little to alter the flow of the game. The next chance came in the 36th minute: Momoko Tanikawa lofted the ball to Dallmann, whose shot inside the box was blocked by the Stuttgart defence. Just before half-time, Tanikawa found herself in space inside the box, but her effort missed the target by just a few centimetres.

Bayern came out firing after the break too: barely 30 seconds had passed when Tanikawa got a shot away in the penalty area following a lay-off from Mattner. However, her attempt to curl the ball into the top corner from a half-right position went just a little too high. In the 49th minute, the hosts got a third: Harder played a pinpoint pass into the channel, Bühl broke clear, rounded goalkeeper Giuliani and slotted the ball comfortably into the empty goal. Just two minutes later, Bayern looked to increase their lead: following a pass from Dallmann, Kett attempted to slot the ball home in the near corner but was just off-target, so Giuliani didn't have to make the save. In the 59th minute, though, it happened again: the agile Dallmann played the ball on to Tanikawa, who carried it forward a few metres and picked out Harder on the left with a precise through pass. The Denmark international first-timed the ball with her right boot, slotting it low into the left corner.

Bayern were now playing with real abandon: Tanikawa tried her luck herself shortly afterwards, but missed the target, as did Dunst, whose shot went too high following a fine run (65'). Just a minute later, Bühl initiated an attack, passing the ball to Tanikawa, who then found Harder, but her effort struck the post. Just before the final whistle, Imade was rewarded for her performance, nodding home from a fine cross from Sophie Proost to make it 5–0 and wrapping up a more than deserved home win in the Südschlager .

Away to Leipzig and at home against Real Madrid

Following their home game against VfB Stuttgart, FC Bayern Women are next in action in the Google Pixel Women's Bundesliga : on Friday 23 October, the Munich side travel to face RB Leipzig at 18:30 CEST. Following that is another highlight in the UEFA Women's Champions League: on Wednesday 28 October, head coach Barcala's side host Real Madrid at Sportpark Unterhaching at 18:45 CEST.

articles.title: Tennessee Has The Best Defense In The Country And Here’s Why
articles.summary: Jim Knowles has completely transformed Tennessee’s defense into a national powerhouse, and the Volunteers might have the most dangerous unit in America. Forg...
articles.body:
Jim Knowles has completely transformed Tennessee's defense into a national powerhouse, and the Volunteers might have the most dangerous unit in America.

Forget Georgia. Forget Ohio State. Forget Alabama.

The best defense in college football might be playing in Knoxville, Tennessee.

Jim Knowles has completely transformed the Volunteers in his first season as defensive coordinator, and Saturday's dominant 26-10 victory over Alabama was the perfect example of just how dangerous this defense has become.

Tennessee absolutely embarrassed the Crimson Tide offensively, holding Alabama to just 201 total yards, forcing four turnovers and recording five sacks. The Volunteers also shut out Alabama throughout the entire second half.

And here's the scary part: This defense might only be getting better.

Tennessee entered Saturday leading the nation with 25 sacks before adding five more against Alabama. Linebacker Jeremiah Telander recorded two sacks, two tackles for loss and a forced fumble, while Tyree Weathersby added two sacks of his own.

The secondary has been just as impressive. Dejuan Lane and Kayin Lee each recorded interceptions against Alabama, making life miserable for freshman quarterback Keelon Russell.

But perhaps the most remarkable part of Tennessee's defensive transformation is how quickly Knowles has accomplished it.

Last season, the Volunteers ranked 92nd nationally in scoring defense and allowed nearly 397 yards per game. Through seven games this season, Tennessee has become one of the most disruptive defensive units in America.

And remember, Knowles helped Ohio State win a national championship with an elite defense before eventually making his way to Knoxville.

Now, he's bringing that same championship mentality to Tennessee.

For years, Josh Heupel's teams have been known for explosive offenses that could score on almost anyone. But defensive inconsistency often prevented the Volunteers from reaching their full potential.

Tennessee sits at 6-1 with legitimate College Football Playoff aspirations, and its defense could be the difference between another good season and a championship run.

The rest of the SEC should be terrified. Tennessee no longer needs to score 40 points to beat elite opponents.

And with Jim Knowles running the defense, the Volunteers might have finally found the missing piece to becoming a national championship contender.

articles.title: Liverpool have incredible new playmaker, he's better than Florian Wirtz
articles.summary: Florian Wirtz is getting better at Liverpool but there's someone ready to takeover from him very soon. It's not quite been the esteem for the German midfield...
articles.body:
Florian Wirtz is getting better at Liverpool but there's someone ready to takeover from him very soon.

It's not quite been the esteem for the German midfielder that he expected when he first arrived at Anfield. Florian Wirtz came with a lot of promise but he hasn't really delivered those expectations.

There have been great performances from the German. But they have also been juxtaposed by some utterly disappointing performances.

On the balance of things, you'd have to say there have been more disappointing performances than great ones so far.

That's a real shame because at one point in time while at Bayer Leverkusen it seemed like Wirtz was heading right to the very top of the game.

He's young, and he still have time of course.

How Liverpool can get the best out of Florian Wirtz

For any playmaker in order for him to function well in a team, he needs to have the right teammates around him. It's impossible for a playmaker to do well if his teammates are not making the right runs.

For a lot of his time at Liverpool Wirtz has had to balanced playing with a wide myriad of attackers. He's had to become accustomed to not just playing with one but multiple different types of players.

That's a factor that will undoubtedly have an impact on his overall performance.

There's also another element at play. A lot of the times, Liverpool cannot find Wirtz in the right areas. There's no coincidence that Wirtz plays better when Trey Nyoni and Jeremy Jacquet are both on the pitch.

The duo are known for their ability to play line-breaking passes and are able to find Wirtz in better positions.

Meet Liverpool's new incredible playmaker - AJ Yeguo

Wirtz's problem is that he didn't grow up in England. He needs a lot more time to acclimatise to English football. That's something AJ Yeguo doesn't have to worry about.

He has been at Liverpool's academy from a young age, and he has also represented both Poland and England's youth national teams.

The young attacker, is only 17-years-old but he's catching the eye for the Reds' academy with his playmaking ability.

He put on a great cameo for Liverpool's U19 side in the UEFA Youth League against LASK and impressed in the U18 Premier League where he has two goals and three assists in just six appearances.

A quick and very physically strong player. Yeguo's creative flair combined with his physical qualities not only make him an incredible playmaker but it could make him better suited to the Premier League in comparison to Wirtz.

articles.title: Marc Guéhi insists Manchester City players 'relaxed' over Premier League charges
articles.summary: Manchester City defender Marc Guéhi has weighed in on the squad's mindset regarding the charges levied against the club, following an independent commission'...
articles.body:
Marc Guéhi says Manchester City players remain composed despite the club being found guilty of cheating, owing to their confidence in what they have been told.

City maintain their innocence regarding breaches of financial regulations and are appealing the verdict - which saw them found guilty on 114 of the 115 charges brought against them by the Premier League - with the squad quickly accepting reassurances from club leadership.

Guéhi is part of the four-man leadership group at the Etihad, having been handpicked by Enzo Maresca during the summer to join the setup. Captain Rúben Dias and his deputy Erling Haaland were both at the club when the charges were first announced in 2023, and have spearheaded calls for the players to channel their energy into winning games.

"The club notified everyone straight away so we were pretty calm," he said, via the Manchester Evening News . "There were a lot of relaxed faces because we have a lot of trust and belief in the club and what's been going on here.

"It's been nice, it's been good. We get to see a lot of togetherness. The team spirit has been really fantastic from every single person and player - especially the staff and the fans that are backing us. To be honest, it's been great to see.

"It can be very easy to listen to the noise and be affected by everything going on but I'm so happy to see the team spirit and everyone taking to what's happening and just focusing on the football."

City brought Guéhi on board during the January transfer window, yet the former Crystal Palace skipper instantly believed the information he received when reports of City's guilty verdict first emerged three weeks ago. The 26-year-old remains committed to being part of the club's future as they fight to reverse the ruling handed down against them.

"Ever since I've got here they've been nothing but fantastic with me," he added. "The support that I've had with tough times on and off the pitch. I'm aware of the success the club has had and I want to be part of the future success. You get the sense from everyone at the football club that it's a family club, people love one another. I can only talk from my experience."

articles.title: Bruce Pearl once told Lane Kiffin Jordan-Hare Stadium was haunted. What the LSU coach thinks
articles.summary: Is Auburn's Jordan-Hare Stadium haunted? Bruce Pearl once tried to sell Lane Kiffin on that. Here's what the LSU football coach thinks of Auburn.
articles.body:
But if you ask Nick Saban , one of Kiffin's coaching mentors, or other coaches or experts have voiced it — there's even been stories written about it recently. Strange things happen inside Jordan-Hare Stadium, Auburn 's home football field.

Some, like Saban, go as far to say, the place is haunted. Kiffin, the first-year LSU football coach, isn't on the "Jordan-Hare Stadium is haunted" bandwagon, but he has another word that he uses to describe the venue.

"I don't think it's haunted, but there's some magical stuff that happens in there," Kiffin told reporters during his weekly press conference Monday, Oct. 19 ahead of his team's road trip to face Auburn this weekend.

The Kick-Six, the Prayer at Jordan-Hare and odd Les Miles clock management moments are the tip of the iceberg of the spooks that have played out inside Auburn's stadium over the years. It's known to be one of the harder places to win a football game, regardless of if Auburn is ranked and playing well or not.

Records don't mean anything inside Jordan-Hare.

Kiffin has been on the opposing sideline three times there and his record is 2-1. The lone loss was in 2021 when he took his 6-1 Ole Miss team in there and faced a good, 5-2 Auburn team and ended up falling short, 31-20.

Photos of LSU Tigers vs Mississippi State Football from Tiger Stadium

"A really electric place. Been there a lot and part of the Iron Bowl. It's kind of a magical place," Kiffin said. "We're going to have to play really well and be ready to play in a really loud environment that they play well at.

"It's always about preparation and preparing really well, practicing really well and then when you go in there, making less mistakes than a lot of the times on the road. As you breakdown your losses and close losses, they're usually not as much about how many plays they make. It's more the mistakes you make, and the penalties, more false starts and more turnovers than when you play at home."

Kiffin was once courted by Auburn to take over the football program a few years back and then men's basketball coach Bruce Pearl tried to sell him on how the place's haunted factor leads to unexpected wins.

"When Auburn was trying to hire me, Bruce Pearl tried to tell me that it was. He's like, 'Hey, you'll get a win every year that you really don't deserve because magical things just happen here,' Kiffin recalled, "'it's haunted.'"

Kiffin and his staff may likely have to bust some ghosts Saturday inside Jordan-Hare Stadium.

articles.title: Ronaldo given 30-day suspension and £215 fine by Portuguese FA
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo is given a 30-day suspension by the Portuguese Football Federation after leaving his country's international camp last month.
articles.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo has been given a 30-day suspension and fined 255 euros (£215) by the Portuguese Football Federation after leaving his country's international camp last month.

The 41-year-old captain walked out of Portugal's Nations League squad in September after being an unused substitute against Norway and then finding out he would not start against Denmark.

Ronaldo said in a lengthy statement he had left because Portugal coach Jorge Jesus twice "broke his word", accusing him of an "absolute breach of trust".

It is not clear which matches or activities the suspension would cover, or whether time already served under a provisional suspension would count towards the 30-day sanction.

The Al-Nassr forward was provisionally suspended on 9 October. If the suspension is backdated to that date, he will be available to play in his country's next match - against Denmark on 14 November.

Portugal boss Jesus denied making any agreement with Ronaldo but has left the door open for his return.

Ronaldo accepted accountability and apologised to his team-mates and fans for his actions, before adding he deserved to be punished.

Pedro Proenca, president of the FPF, told Portuguese outlet Record there is a "strong desire" to have Ronaldo back with the national team once the matter is resolved.

Ronaldo, who has won the Ballon d'Or five times, has scored 146 goals in 234 Portugal appearances - both men's world records - helping them win Euro 2016 and the two Nations League titles.

articles.title: Uefa gives Infantino two-week deadline to release key documents
articles.summary: Uefa's letter contained 42 questions, covering Fifa's failed private investment proposals, its Peace Prize and the fallout from Folarin Balogun's World Cup r...
articles.body:
European governing body Uefa has told Fifa it must release key documents and answer all questions relating to its governance and decision-making by a deadline of 2 November.

At the Fifa Council on Thursday, president Gianni Infantino apologised for his World Cup sell-off plan - but failed to offer a full explanation for how the proposal was devised.

In the letter seen by BBC Sport, Uefa general secretary Theodore Theodoridis said that world football's governing body had failed to address "a number of fundamental questions".

"Others remain unanswered, and the information and documentation requested have not been provided," it read.

The letter included eight pages containing 42 questions covering a number of issues, from the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) private investment, to the Fifa Peace Prize and the controversial suspended ban given to USA striker Folarin Balogun at the World Cup.

"The withdrawal of FFE, the acknowledgement of mistakes and the announcement of 'potential governance reforms' do not answer how the relevant decisions were taken or why the Fifa Council was not involved at the appropriate stage," it continued.

"Any refusal to disclose information or documents should be justified individually, with a clear explanation of the specific grounds relied upon.

"These questions require answers now. They cannot be deferred until the next meeting of the Fifa Council - nor can future governance reforms substitute for scrutiny of decisions already taken and accountability for them."

Uefa did not outline what steps it intended to take should Fifa not meet the deadline.

The questions were first put to Infantino at the Fifa Council last week, with Infantino then asking that they were submitted in writing.

Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt - a Fifa vice-president - said afterwards that "if he doesn't answer those questions, he's not fit to be Fifa president".

Fifa faces question on FFE and funding to associations

Uefa has posed a great number of questions about FFE.

"When was the idea of FFE first explored, by whom and with what objective?" Uefa asked. "Who within Fifa authorised the development of the project, and which members of the Fifa administration were involved?

"What concrete measures will Fifa put in place to ensure that the shortcomings identified in the FFE process cannot occur again in the future?"

Uefa goes on to ask about the circumstances surrounding Infantino's initial presentation of the FFE plan to senior Fifa executives.

In particular, it raises a question about a potential investigation into Fifa in the United States. BBC Sport has approached Uefa to ascertain what this is in relation to.

"According to information received from several sources, two days before the vote by the bureau of the management board on the FFE proposal, the Fifa president informed members of the management board that the US authorities were investigating Fifa's administration," Uefa claim.

"Can he confirm whether such a statement was made and, if so, explain the information on which it was based, the reasons for raising it at that particular moment and whether he considered the potential pressure it might place on members immediately before their decision on FFE?"

Uefa requested information on whether Infantino would have held or expected to hold any position, role or function in FFE, either during or following his tenure as Fifa president.

The relationship with Joshua Kushner's Thrive Capital was covered in detail, asking why an agreement granting exclusivity to the company was signed without prior consultation of the Fifa Council.

"Why was Thrive Capital selected as lead investor, without any competitive tendering process and under conditions of strict confidentiality, despite its links to the family of the recipient of the Fifa Peace Prize?" Uefa asked.

Kushner is the brother of Donald Trump's son-in-law, while the US president was awarded the Peace Prize.

Uefa also requested answer about the award of the Peace Prize, specifically who decided to establish it, for what purpose, and who decided that Trump should receive it.

When the FFE plan was revealed in the days following the World Cup final, Infantino told the 211 member associations (MAs) they would receive $40m (£30m) if they backed it. He then set a deadline of 19 September for federations to accept his plans if they wanted to access an initial $20m (£15m).

However, once the scheme was abandoned, Uefa and Concacaf called on Fifa to pay at least $10m (£7.5m) from its cash reserves to each of the MAs and, last week, Infantino agreed, proposing to increase the amount of money handed out for football development across the world by $3.4bn (£2.6bn).

The releasing of cash from its reserves will result in double the level of planned distribution funding for MAs from 2027 to 2030, with $25m (£19m) available per member association.

"Why was substantially increased funding for MAs presented in connection with FFE and external investment, rather than being financed directly from Fifa's own resources?" Uefa has asked.

"Given Fifa's strong financial position, why was it considered necessary to seek investment from private investors? What financial or strategic advantages would such an arrangement have offered compared with funding football development directly from Fifa's own resources, particularly in light of Fifa's subsequent proposal to do precisely that on a substantially increased scale?"

While Fifa is yet to respond, sources have indicated its ability to answer certain questions are restricted by the legal action that Uefa has launched. Last month, it filed legal papers in the US requesting disclosure of evidence and documents from Fifa, warning it could lodge a criminal complaint in Switzerland.

Uefa wants answers over Balogun suspension

Infantino has faced intense scrutiny over the case of Balogun, who avoided an immediate suspension after being sent off at the World Cup.

Balogun's ban was lifted by Fifa's disciplinary committee, after US President Donald Trump asked Infantino for the decision to be reviewed.

Fifa insisted the committee was independent but its legal committee is now reviewing a proposal to amend its disciplinary code, which would prevent a repeat, with an update due in December. Uefa has asked why this is necessary.

"President Trump publicly acknowledged having called the Fifa president to request a review of the Balogun disciplinary case. What exactly did he ask him to do, and what was his response?", Uefa has asked. "Would the case have been reviewed in the absence of his intervention?"

"Following that conversation, did the Fifa president or the Fifa secretary general communicate with anyone within Fifa, including members of the administration or the chair of the disciplinary committee, concerning the Balogun case? If so, could Fifa specify with whom, when and the nature of those communications?

"We also request all correspondence and other communications concerning the case between the chair of the disciplinary committee and the Fifa administration, including the Fifa president and Fifa's chief legal officer.

"Could Fifa provide the full written reasons for the decision in the Balogun case, including the information and evidence before the disciplinary committee?

"Who decided that the matter should be determined by a single member of the committee, on what basis…and what were the exceptional circumstances relied upon to justify the decision?"

Uefa also asked why no disciplinary action was taken against DR Congo after the African nation reportedly played an ineligible player in World Cup qualifying. Usually, this would result in the country being disqualified but no action was taken.

Infantino quizzed over additional salary

Reports in the lead-up last week's Fifa Council suggested Infantino had received an additional salary from Fifa's US World Cup organising entity (FWC2026 US Inc.) which was not disclosed in Fifa's annual report.

Uefa has asked Fifa to "clarify the nature, amount and basis of these payments, why they were not disclosed and whether they were reviewed and approved by the competent Fifa bodies."

It added: "Could Fifa also confirm whether the additional remuneration was treated as taxable income and whether the corresponding income tax was paid?"

Fifa has previously denied paying Infantino a second salary, and insisted it complies with all reporting requirements in relation to compensation, saying it "strongly rejects any claims that it has failed to disclose any financial information and has violated Fifa's statutes."

Uefa also asked about reported "advanced discussions involving the US president and individuals associated with him concerning a Fifa cryptocurrency", and the $75m (£56.3m) investment in Palestine via Trump's Board of Peace.

The extended 27-minute half-time interval during the World Cup final and introduction of mandatory hydration breaks were also raised.

Uefa wanted answers on the "seven-year, $4m (£3m) lease of office premises in Trump Tower, New York, involving Eric Trump, for premises reportedly unused for much of the year".

It wrote: "These matters, taken together, raise questions that extend beyond the ordinary institutional relationship between Fifa and the government of a World Cup host country.

"Could Fifa provide a detailed explanation of these arrangements and interventions, including the decision-making processes followed, the identification and management of any potential conflicts of interest, the financial implications for Fifa and the extent to which the competent Fifa bodies were informed or consulted?"

Also brought up was the impartiality of the chair of the Fifa electoral committee before next year's presidential election who, Uefa says, "attended the entire 2026 World Cup as an accredited individual, with his expenses covered by Fifa for more than five weeks".

It also asked for a full list of the guests seated in the VIP and VVIP sections "including their names, positions and the reasons for their invitations".

articles.title: Chelsea Are Keeping Tabs On This Talented Midfielder: Should Alonso Snap Him Up?
articles.summary: In a recent report, journalist Graeme Bailey mentioned that Chelsea are keeping tabs on Goteborg midfielder Oliver Mansson. It has been claimed that the Blue...
articles.body:
In a recent report , journalist Graeme Bailey mentioned that Chelsea are keeping tabs on Goteborg midfielder Oliver Mansson. It has been claimed that the Blues are eyeing a move to recruit the Swedish talent next year.

Mansson's Impressive Rise In Swedish Football

Mansson has come through the youth ranks of Goteborg and has done well to establish himself as an important member of their senior team. The 17-year-old has made 13 league appearances for the Swedish outfit, securing three assists in the process.

The talented teenager is currently among the most gifted midfielders in the Allsvenskan. Hence, it is no wonder that the Blues are eyeing a move to bring him to Stamford Bridge next year.

However, Mansson is still quite raw and would need time to prove his worth at the highest level. Plus, there are some concerns over whether he can cope with the physical side and high intensity of the Premier League if Chelsea manage to acquire his services next year.

LIVERPOOL, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 17: Xabi Alonso, Manager of Chelsea, looks on as players of Chelsea acknowledge the fans after during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Everton and Chelsea FC at Hill Dickinson Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Liverpool, England. (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

Should Chelsea Boss Xabi Alonso Snap Mansson Up?

Mansson works hard for his team defensively when needed and is a tidy passer as well from midfield. He can shoot the ball well from long range and has the vision to engineer some promising chances for his teammates in the final third.

The Swedish sensation is full of energy and running at the centre of the park and can chip in by picking up his fair share of assists from midfield. Mansson is primarily a box-to-box midfielder but can also serve as a defensive midfielder if required. However, it remains to be seen whether he can make a smooth transition to life in the Premier League if the Blues manage to snap him up next year.

We can expect Mansson to add more quality to Chelsea's academy. He has the potential to be a future star at Stamford Bridge as long as he continues to improve with each year.

At 17, Mansson is a generational talent, so Xabi Alonso would be wise to go all out to snap him up this winter or at the end of this season. However, the Blues have to give him some time to adjust to life in England before they can get the best out of the player.

articles.body: LaLiga publicó un vídeo donde recogió las imágenes más destacadas de la 'RefCam' que llevaba Ricardo De Burgos Bengoetxea durante el Betis-Barcelona. Un vídeo en el que destaca la acción del gol anulado a Lo Celso, en el que el colegiado habló con futbolistas de ambos equipos, que le contaban sus impresiones de la jugada. "Chequéame la mano, que es lo que me piden, Cerro", dice De Burgos a Carlos Del Cerro Grande, responsable del VAR en ese encuentro. Una frase que ha conllevado alguna crítica, como la de Iturralde González, que en su cuenta de X escribió: "Acabamos de descubrir el VAR a la carta. Chequéame esto que me piden". El exárbitro entiende que los colegiados de campo no pueden pedir a los de VAR que se revise una acción en concreto, sino que tiene que ser desde la sala VOR desde donde avisen si hay algo irregular. Más allá de esa frase, los jugadores del Barcelona, con Pedri y Rodri a la cabeza, insisten a De Burgos en que la mano del Cucho es muy clara. "A mí no me parece punible", insiste el árbitro, que espera a que desde el VAR le indiquen si tiene que ir a revisarla o no. En plena espera se acerca Héctor Bellerín para soltar un curioso argumento para no anular el gol, que no tiene que ver con el reglamento sino con la belleza del gol. "Sólo por el gol que ha metido hay que dejarla. Sólo por el gol que ha metido hay que dejarlo, por el fútbol".

articles.title: Chendo, a Mbappé en el banquillo: "¿Sabes lo que significa 'polaco'?"

articles.body: Las cámaras de 'El Día Después' captaron la conversación entre Chendo y Kylian Mbappé en el banquillo, después de que el francés fuera sustituido contra el Sevilla en los últimos minutos del partido, ya con 4-1 en el marcador con un doblete del '10' madridista. A los pocos segundos de sentarse en el banquillo, una parte de la afición madridista canta "¡Es polaco el que no bote!", uno de los cánticos que se utilizan para insultar a los aficionados del Barcelona. Acto seguido, Chendo le dice a Mbappé: "¿Sabes lo que significa 'polaco'?". "¿Las canciones?", pregunta Kylian. Después, ya con la boca tapada, Chendo le vuelve a decir algo y terminan riéndose. articles.title: Kiper Says Arch Manning Should Be Backup for 3 Years If QB Enters NFL Draft, Follow Packers Model
articles.summary: Arch Manning may be the biggest name in college football given his namesake and position as the starting quarterback for Texas, but his draft outlook could be slipping.
articles.body:
Arch Manning may be the biggest name in college football given his namesake and position as the starting quarterback for Texas, but his draft outlook could be slipping.

"All I'll say is right now, you gotta go back to college for another year," ESPN's Mel Kiper Jr. said of Manning ahead of the 2027 NFL draft (36:15 mark). "And if you don't, it's got to be the Green Bay Packer model of Jordan Love and Aaron Rodgers where you got your guy and you're picking late first round and you got your quarterback for another three years.

Arch Manning's tenure with Texas may be nearing end

"I'm saying three years, I'm not saying one, not saying two. Patrick Mahomes sat for a year, okay, so let's forget the year. For Arch, I think it's three years. It's gotta be the Jordan Love, Aaron Rodgers, Green Bay Packers model if he comes out."

Manning, who is the nephew of NFL legends Peyton and Eli Manning, has been up and down all season for the Longhorns.

While he directed a thrilling fourth-quarter comeback against Ohio State in the early going, he struggled for much of that game until the end. He then threw an interception without a single touchdown against Tennessee before throwing two costly picks in the rivalry loss to Oklahoma.

One of those interceptions was returned for a touchdown, while the other set up the Sooners' game-winning field goal in the final minute.

Manning was under the microscope for Saturday's game against Florida after that performance and responded with a 27-24 loss that saw him account for just one touchdown.

It's reached a point that head coach Steve Sarkisian had to tell reporters Monday that Manning will remain the team's starter after ESPN's Pete Thamel reported redshirt freshman KJ Lacey Jr. was expected to see an "uptick in first-team quarterback reps" in practice in "a signal that Texas could replace Manning if he continues to struggle."

Had Manning had a dominant 2026 campaign, he could have played his way into discussions to be the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft. His namesake alone would have caught the attention of NFL teams, and thriving under the spotlight at Texas would have bolstered his standing.

However, now one of the most prominent draft experts believes it would be in his best interest to return to school.

articles.title: Diomande y el precio del ruido
articles.standfirst: El extremo marfileño empieza a soltarse con continuidad y a responder sobre el césped a la presión de ser el fichaje más caro de la historia del Madrid
articles.summary: El extremo marfileño empieza a soltarse con continuidad y a responder sobre el césped a la presión de ser el fichaje más caro de la historia del Madrid
articles.body: A Yan Diomande le ha pesado el precio. No es fácil llegar al Real Madrid con la etiqueta de fichaje más caro de su historia, menos aún cuando se tienen 19 años y casi todo por demostrar. Quizá por eso su adaptación ha sido más lenta de lo que muchos esperaban. Quienes apenas le habían visto más allá del Mundial y de sus diez partidos en el Leganés se encontraron de repente con una cifra: 125 millones de euros. Y a partir de ahí, las expectativas se dispararon... y el madridismo empezó a fantasear. Pero el fútbol no funciona así. "En vez de jugar con el 25, juega con el 125 de lo que se ha pagado", explicó Mourinho tras su último gran partido. El portugués no escondió sus carencias ("es joven, es ingenuo, un producto no acabado"), pero tampoco perdió de vista el talento que hay detrás. "Me recuerda a Vinicius cuando llegó al Madrid y tres años más tarde era un jugador de altísimo nivel", añadió. Un mensaje que trata de hacer entender que a Diomande hay que darle tiempo para que deje de jugar condicionado por su propio precio. Porque, cuando encuentra continuidad, el marfileño empieza a parecerse al futbolista que convenció al Madrid para apostar por él. En los últimos tres partidos, en los que ha sido titular, ha marcado dos goles y repartido dos asistencias. Pero su impacto no se mide únicamente en el marcador. Diomande completa 4,9 regates por cada 90 minutos, con un 66,7 % de éxito, y provoca 2,65 faltas en ese mismo intervalo. Se ha convertido en un jugador capaz de desordenar defensas, obligar al rival a multiplicar las ayudas y abrir espacios para sus compañeros. Según los datos de FotMob, es el madridista que más regates completa por minuto de juego, por delante de Mbappé, Bellingham, Vinicius y Arda Güler. La sanción de Vinicius le ha abierto un hueco que Diomande ha sabido aprovechar. La continuidad le ha permitido ganar confianza y los números empiezan a acompañarle. Aunque quizás es más importante las sensaciones que transmite y su gestualidad sobre el césped. Ahora le espera el Clásico, el escenario perfecto para medir su crecimiento y seguir ganando terreno en el Madrid. También hay algo simbólico en su celebración más reciente: el gesto de silencio popularizado por LeBron James. Ambos coincidieron este verano en Estados Unidos, en un evento del rapero Jay-Z, y Diomande ha llevado ese guiño a un escenario muy distinto. Y es que el ruido sigue ahí, pero ya no parece ocupar todo el espacio.

articles.title: Tottenham 3-1 Coventry: Dejan Kulusevski returns to action as Spurs secure first Premier League win of the season
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Tottenham beat Coventry 3-1 at home; Spurs secure first win of the Premier League season thanks to goals from James Maddison, Omar Marmoush and Ben Davies; Jack Rudoni netted for Coventry; Dejan Kulusevski made his return after 526 days sidelined
articles.body:
Spurs were winless across their opening six games heading into this fixture but a week in the Marbella sunshine and a well-needed performance on home turf have helped address the doom and gloom, with brighter skies in N17 possibly on the horizon.

James Maddison, making his first competitive start for Spurs since May 2025, announced his return to the starting line-up in emphatic style, curling his opener into the top corner against the club where his professional career began.

The playmaker was influential throughout, seamlessly linking the £300m pieces of Roberto De Zerbi's squad that had previously looked disjointed and awkward, but Jack Rudoni's equaliser just four minutes into the second half punctured the positivity brewing inside the stadium.

No side has dropped more points than Spurs from winning positions at home in the Premier League since the start of the 2024/25 season (30), but Omar Marmoush's first goal for the club, arrowing a fine strike into the far corner, put them on track to ensure they would not suffer the same fate on this occasion.

The feelgood factor that comes with a win skyrocketed in the 85th minute when fan-favourite Kulusevski made his comeback off the bench, bringing an end to his lengthy spell on the sidelines.

Ben Davies' surprise effort with the outside of the boot rounded off the victory, on what could prove to be the evening that kickstarted the 2026/27 season for Spurs.

They move level on six points with Coventry and above their opponents on goal difference into 16th, having previously come into the fixture rock bottom of the table, and will now be tasked with building on their victory against London rivals Chelsea when the two sides meet at Stamford Bridge, live on Saturday Night Football.

14: GOAL! Maddison curls stunning opener into the top corner on his return to the starting line-up.

18: NO GOA L! Dominic Solanke taps home Andy Robertson's cross but the offside flag had already gone up.

49: EQUALISER! Rudoni powers his way into the Tottenham penalty area to force an equaliser home after half-time.

58: GOAL! Marmoush restores Tottenham's lead with his first goal for the club as his fine strike nestles into the far corner.

86: KULU RETURNS! Spurs winger Kulusevski makes his long-awaited return to the pitch after 526 days out injured with a knee setback.

90+6: GAME OVER! Davies scores a surprise goal off the bench to guarantee Spurs' first league win of the season.

Is Maddison the missing piece that can link the £300m puzzle?

"James Maddison was the star of the show and a big reason Spurs were able to secure the well-needed win. His goal speaks for itself.

"But the rest of his play also stood out, in a slightly more understated manner.

"He was dropping deep, finding pockets of space, threading passes for the runs of Dominic Solanke and threatening from the half spaces with his crossing ability.

"Spurs, after all their investment in the summer, looked disjointed and uninspiring across the opening six games.

"Maddison looks like the piece that could link the £300m pieces of this Spurs puzzle together. Whether that is through his own finishing or the ability to bring other players into the game.

"Keeping him fit and firing is now essential to the club building on this game."

Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher on Monday Night Football:

"James Maddison definitely has more panache than Conor Gallagher in that No 10 position.

"It was a joy to see [his goal]. He is one of the real characters in the game and you don't want him not around Premier League football.

"That was just a great moment. When you're a player with an injury like that, there will be a fear: will you ever come back or will you be the same player?

"There is still a long way to go, but he still has a bit of magic in his boots!"

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Álvaro 'vuela' sobre el Coliseum
articles.standfirst: El extremo franjirrojo abrió el marcador ante el Getafe y causó estragos gracias a su velocidad
articles.summary: El extremo franjirrojo abrió el marcador ante el Getafe y causó estragos gracias a su velocidad
articles.body: Álvaro García no ha ganado seis Champions, pero fue un 'dolor de cabeza' constante para Dani Carvajal. El de Leganés hizo su debut con el Getafe ante el Rayo Vallecano y sufrió para parar al utrerano. Un césped mojado y unas 'flechas' por las bandas (como lo son los extremos del cuadro franjirrojo) forzaron ambos costados hasta llevar al límite a la defensa azulona. El Rayo es un equipo vertical que le va lo de atacar por las bandas. Ya en el minuto 9 llegó el primer relámpago con ambos laterales azulones en la foto. Lejeune recuperó sobre Unal y vio cómo De Frutos corrió hacia arriba. Mojica no le alcanzó, como tampoco lo hizo Carvajal a Álvaro. El segoviano vio a su compañero y el ex del Cádiz hizo el gol. A pesar de la rivalidad entre Carvajal y Álvaro, todo quedó dentro del campo. Ambos protagonizaron una imagen muy amistosa al término del encuentro en la que ambos conversaban con una sonrisa. El utrerano, que ya lleva 51 goles con el Rayo Vallecano, es vital en el esquema rayista. Además del gol, también provocó la expulsión de Djene. Esta vez, sin rastro de Carvajal, Álvaro le ganó la espalda al togolés que lo derribó sin ninguna opción de tocar la pelota. Dos acciones de mucho nivel y sobre todo velocidad que ayudaron al Rayo a mantenerse décimo tercero con una jornada menos.

articles.title: Bordalás: “Carvajal lo ha ganado todo y esa humildad y sencillez ha calado, tiene el cariño de todos”
articles.standfirst: El entrenador azulón comparecía en sala de prensa tras el empate frente al Rayo Vallecano
articles.summary: El entrenador azulón comparecía en sala de prensa tras el empate frente al Rayo Vallecano
articles.body: El técnico del Getafe, José Bordalás, comparecía en sala de prensa tras el empate frente al Rayo Vallecano. El alicantino habló del debut de Carvajal y señaló que el equipo ha hecho un gran esfuerzo para lograr el empate a pesar de la expulsión de Djené en la primera mitad. Mensaje a Valencia: “Quería mandar un mensaje de apoyo y de ánimo a la gente de Valencia, a los familiares de los fallecidos. Es mi gente y sé que están sufriendo mucho”. Empate: “No estamos del todo contentos. El equipo ha hecho un gran esfuerzo, se ha rehecho, ha sido un ejercicio de supervivencia nuevamente. Son muchas expulsiones, tenemos que corregirlo de manera inmediata, no lo podemos permitir. Resaltar que el equipo nunca bajó los brazos. Todo el mundo sabe que hemos hecho un esfuerzo muy grande, venimos del jueves”. Bajas: “Cualquier baja es muy importante, puesto que estamos jugando dos competiciones ahora. Son partidos de mucha exigencia. Ahora la de Djené será una baja importante. Cualquier jugador que recuperemos será importante. Está trabajando el cuerpo técnico a marchas forzadas para intentar que lleguen”. Carvajal: “Muy bien, le tengo que felicitar. Es un profesional, no lo digo yo, es un profesional y lo lleva demostrando toda su carrera, íntegro. Se ha integrado muy rápido, es un líder. Una pena habernos quedado con uno menos porque el esfuerzo ha tenido que ser mayor. A él le ha pasado factura, como a algunos compañeros. Le he visto muy bien, muy contento de tenerle. Todos los compañeros, el grupo, el equipo, estamos muy contentos. Nos va a dar muchísimo durante la temporada. Es un gran líder”. Cambios: “Hemos hecho cambios, hemos intentado estar más juntos. Hemos tenido en el primer tiempo pérdidas muy forzadas que han beneficiado al Rayo. Esas pérdidas nos han condenado en la expulsión, ha sido otra contra. Hemos intentado que el equipo estuviera más junto, que no tuvieran espacios para correr, intentar sacar centros. Hay que mejorar en eso porque tenemos buenos rematadores. Nos faltan jugadores de juego exterior. Tenemos buenos jugadores en los laterales, hay que aprovechar nuestras virtudes, que las tenemos. El equipo sabía que tenía que hacer un esfuerzo extra, ha creído”. Vestuario con Carvajal: “Es un chaval con una humildad y una sencillez que te llama la atención. Ha ganado muchísimos títulos, ha estado en el Real Madrid toda su carrera menos un año, lo ha ganado todo y esa humildad y sencillez ha calado. Le admiramos, rápidamente se ha ganado el cariño de todos”. 21 faltas y diez cartulinas: “Opinad vosotros, estoy de acuerdo. Se sacan demasiadas tarjetas y nosotros llevábamos dos tarjetas en muy pocos minutos, una a Kiko en el minuto uno y otra a Djené en una mano que no podía cortársela. Se llevan temporadas así, no estoy de acuerdo con ello. Si comparamos con la Premier, que es una de las mejores ligas, aquí se sacan dos veces más, es una barbaridad. Yo entiendo que el instinto es proteger la integridad”. Terrats: “Tienes que sacrificar a un jugador porque te han expulsado a un central. A cualquiera no le sienta bien. Protegerle, él venía de jugar el jueves, tuvo un golpe muy fuerte en el hombro que lo ha tenido muy preocupado a él y a todos. Tenía molestias, se ha tenido que infiltrar antes. Era el cambio para cuidarle a él. Era el cambio que tocaba en ese momento”.

articles.title: Spurs 3-1 Coventry: James Maddison shines on Tottenham return
articles.summary: On his first start since May 2025, James Maddison provided the moment of magic Tottenham were waiting for in their 3-1 victory against Coventry, writes Phil McNulty.
articles.body:
Roberto de Zerbi has used all the tools at his disposal to discover the missing spark in struggling Tottenham Hotspur , from acting as an amateur psychologist to team bonding dinners, then a sunshine break in Marbella.

The answer, at least when Spurs finally moved off the bottom of the table with their first Premier League win this season against Coventry City , came in the shape of James Maddison as he made his first start in 18 months.

He missed most of last season after suffering an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury in pre-season, before fracturing his shoulder in the opening-weekend defeat at Brentford in this campaign.

The 29-year-old finally made it back into the Spurs starting line-up to face Coventry - and delivered in spectacular style to set them on the way to a 3-1 victory that De Zerbi hopes will finally give their season lift-off.

Maddison could barely keep the smile from his face as he warmed up, then made his mark in the 14th minute by showing what Spurs have been missing with a brilliant right-foot finish from 20 yards, taking Mohammed Kudus' pass first time to arc a sweeping strike high beyond Coventry City keeper Carl Rushworth.

It was a moment of sweet relief for Maddison, the goal getting loud gasps of admiration from Spurs supporters as it was shown several times on the stadium's big screens.

Maddison shines on return - Tottenham v Coventry ratings

Tottenham overcome Coventry to end winless start

Even though the goal came against his former club, Maddison celebrated with his trademark imaginary dart throwing motion before kissing the badge on his Spurs shirt.

Maddison's significance to Spurs is illustrated by the fact they had won just 12 out of 57 Premier League games since his last top-flight goal, in a 1-0 victory against Manchester United in February 2025. They had averaged less than a point a game since then.

And since his last start, at Liverpool on 27 April 2025, Spurs had won only 11 of 49 league games in between, losing 23.

Spurs cannot kid themselves that this was a glorious victory. It was actually only their sixth win in the past 37 home league games - drawing 10 and losing 21 - and just their fourth league victory overall in 2026, having played 27, drawn 10 and lost 13.

And it was the first time they scored three goals or more at home in the league since the opening day of last season, when they beat Burnley 3-0 in Thomas Frank's first game in charge.

There are still too many nerves around Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and in De Zerbi's team for calm and relaxation.

The victory margin flattered them somewhat, with Jack Rudoni equalising for Coventry City before Omar Marmoush's strike for his first goal for the club, then another from Ben Davies in stoppage time after a dreadful Rushworth error finally allowed Spurs to enjoy the relief of victory.

And there were other things to celebrate. As well as Maddison's successful return to the starting line-up, there was the sight of Dejan Kulusevski finally back as an 87th-minute replacement for Kudus after 526 days out with a knee injury.

Maddison got a deserved standing ovation when he was substituted for Conor Gallagher after 69 minutes, but the reception for Kulusevski was arguably even more rapturous as he finally took to the pitch again after such a long battle to regain fitness.

It was Maddison, however, who claimed the major plaudits after he was the driving force behind the win that has proved so elusive - his positive approach playing with a smile on his face provides refreshment of its own after such a depressing sequence of results.

He was eager to get on the ball, was constantly probing and prompting, all before he inevitably tired after the break.

"I spoke to the gaffer this weekend about it, feeling like it was the right moment for me to go back into the starting XI after a bit of a stop-start start to the season," Maddison told Sky Sports.

"I just wanted to play well and show my abilities, show what the team has missed the last 18 months. The gaffer asked me to play and wanted to enjoy watching from the side. Hopefully I did that, and a goal is always nice."

If his aim was to show what Spurs have been missing, this was very much mission accomplished.

And as well as Maddison and Kulusevski, Marmoush will gain confidence from his strike, another superb curling effort that gave Rushworth no chance.

De Zerbi will know this is only a start, with a tough trip to face Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday evening (17:30 BST).

He welcomed the return of Maddison and Kulusevski, saying: "They are different players, different talents, different personalities. With them in the dressing room there is a different atmosphere."

What changes the atmosphere in the dressing room and beyond most are victories.

Now De Zerbi and Spurs can actually build on three points at last, and the sights of Maddison and Kulusevski back in action will have the Italian hoping they can accelerate an improvement after the misery of recent times.

articles.title: Fede, el clásico dilema
articles.standfirst: La posición del capitán, presumiblemente de nuevo en banda, apunta a ser una de las claves del Real Madrid en su vista al Barça
articles.summary: La posición del capitán, presumiblemente de nuevo en banda, apunta a ser una de las claves del Real Madrid en su vista al Barça
articles.body: El partido ante el Sevilla dejó varias noticias para el Real Madrid. Una de las mejores fue el rendimiento de Fede Valverde, de nuevo como lateral derecho tras los buenos minutos del capitán en esa posición en la remontada de Champions ante la Roma. Ante el Sevilla, el uruguayo inició el partido como 2 y completó una actuación sólida, que le perfila como una alternativa más que válida en una demarcación en la que ni Trent ni Dumfries están obteniendo unanimidad. El holandés apunta a ser titular en el carril derecho ante el RB Leipzig, pero la gran incógnita a estas alturas apunta a la ubicación de Fede en el clásico del próximo domingo en Barcelona. A expensas de lo que pueda ocurrir en el partido de Champions de este miércoles, todo apunta a que Fede volverá a jugar en banda en en el Camp Nou. El rendimiento de Arda en el doble pivote es la mejor garantía de generación de fútbol por parte del Madrid, con Tchouaméni como guardaespaldas del turco. A partir de ahi, la duda no apunta tanto al perfil que ocupará Valverde ante el líder como a su altura. La opción de que repita como lateral está sobre la mesa, pero no es descartable que adelante su posición para jugar como falso extremo derecho, formando un doble lateral, posiblemente con Dumfries como pareja. Será una alternativa factible dado que parece difícil que Mou se atreva de nuevo con Endrick como extremo derecho ante el Barcelona. El brasileño es, a estas alturas de su carrera, más un revulsivo (como se demostró en Roma), que una alternativa consistente como titular. La ubicación de Fede como extremo no sería nueva para él, ya que ha ocupado esa posición en muchos partidos de su carrera en el Madrid, especialmente con Carlo Ancelotti. Con el blindaje de Dumfries por detrás, el charrúa tendría libertad para atacar los espacios, el aspecto del juego en el que más destaca gracias a su potencia y zancada. La polivalencia es otra de sus grandes virtudes, un recurso que Mou, al igual que sus predecesores en el banquillo del Bernabéu, están sabiendo explotar, algo que parece empezar a ser asumido por el futbolista. "Lo importante -dijo tras la victoria de Champions en Roma- es ganar, como dijo el míster, si las cosas salen bien hay que salir adelante y yo feliz de seguir teniendo minutos sea donde sea, disfruto mucho jugando, tenía mucho espacio para correr en banda y agradecido a que el míster siga confiando en mí y yo daré el máximo por el equipo".

articles.title: Chad Johnson Offers Jesse Legree $2M in NIL to Stay at Oregon State, WR Leads NCAA in Yards and TDs
articles.summary: Wide receiver Jesse Legree has had a tremendous freshman season at Oregon State, but naturally, the conversation surrounding him has been more about where he'll end up in the transfer portal.
articles.body:
Wide receiver Jesse Legree has had a tremendous freshman season at Oregon State, but naturally, the conversation surrounding him has been more about where he'll end up in the transfer portal.

Chad Johnson is hoping he can outbid top schools that try to lure Legree away from Corvallis. Johnson, who played college football at Oregon State, told head coach JaMarcus Shepard that he'll match a $2 million payment to Legree.

"Hey (JaMarcus Shepard), you give him $2 million, I give him $2 million. That's $4 million right there," Johnson said on his podcast, Nightcap Show.

8 Overreactions after Week 7 of CFB Season 😬

Legree was just a 3-star prospect coming out of high school, but has quickly proved to be one of the best receivers in college football. He currently leads the nation in receiving yards (1,040) and receiving touchdowns (14). The only receiver even close to him is Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith, a Heisman Trophy candidate.

Since Oregon State is a smaller program compared to the Texas, Georgia and Ohio States of the world, it's fair to assume the Beavers will be outbid if and when Legree hits the portal this offseason.

But perhaps Johnson's donation will help convince him to stay at Oregon State.
